utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we stop there, then. So that was the talk show, public from Television Zagreb. The name of the programme was Ukrupni [phoen] Plan, or Close-Up. It took place in 1992, with the participation of Minister Gojko Susak, who, asked by a viewer, answered in public as he did. General Slobodan Praljak sat next to him, and other high-ranking officers of the then HV took part in the programme. I just wish to illustrate what I have been saying hitherto and something that we shall present before the Court by way of evidence. Now we come to my final explanation of how people were coming from Croatia and other countries throughout the world, and we come to my client, and I'm now going to focus on my client, the accused. Let me remind you. Mr. Mladen Naletilic, with pride, said the following sentence at his Initial Appearance: "If it is a crime to defend one's homeland, then I am guilty." By saying that, he meant that it was his duty and that he was honour-bound, like all others, led by the noble goal of defending his homeland, both in the Republic of Croatia and in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to defend his family and threshold. And that is not a crime; it is his duty and an honour to do so, and he went there to perform his duty and not to commit a crime. My client, Mladen Naletilic, left his family and all the comforts of the type of life he led in the Federal Republic of Germany to come to the Republic of Croatia and then to go to Siroki Brijeg, which at the time was under imminent danger of being occupied by the JNA. We shall move to show, through our evidence, that he would have been a moral zero, if I can put it that way, had he not taken that moral step and taken part, as one of the founders of a unit which got the name of the Convicts' Battalion, and along with him it was formed by the former convicts of their own ideals and consciences who were persecuted by the Communist regime in the former Yugoslavia. And the unit, together with the other units that were formed, had the important role to liberate Mostar and the whole of Herzegovina, and had many victims and casualties on the way, and it also took part in the first victory against the army of Republika Srpska. He himself was born at Siroki Brijeg. He was therefore a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But he never took out a Bosnia-Herzegovinian passport, so he was the citizen of Croatia, in fact, a citizen of Croatia. I'm going to skip over the next part and take up my story here. In the indictment we see that when the HVO is mentioned, when reference is made to the HVO, it says that the propaganda of -- that certain circles, in order to realise their political goals, intentionally showed this situation to be -- showed the situation in a different light, and many international representatives, unfortunately, although with very meager arguments or negligible arguments -- we saw a vehicle with HV number plates or a general that we assumed was a general of the HV, although the Defence will show that the general that Mr. McGrinton [phoen], the public witness, spoke to was a general of the HVO and not the HV. And who rode in those cars, although they had HV number plates, remains unclear. And once again, there is silence on the agreement between the BiH and RH states that I mentioned a moment ago. The International Community and the United Nations, let me repeat, recognised the external borders, whereas the internal political order and system was to be agreed upon later on. Mr. Izetbegovic used this to show the Muslims and the army of BiH as the sole legitimate representatives of that state, although those organs of power and authority were made up of Muslims exclusively, without the presence of the other peoples and other ethnic groups, and as such they were illegitimate, illegal, because in a state of equal peoples they should all have taken part on a basis of equality. And for illustration purposes, let me say it's the same thing as if you had a three-storey house with three brothers living in it, then you have to divide up the house amongst those three brothers. So that is what the situation was like, and that's when the International Community came into play. Every plan - Cutilliero's plan, the Vance-Owen Plan, the Owen-Stoltenberg plan, and later the Washington Agreement, which was to realise this - always went in line with the division of Bosnia, the just division of Bosnia, guided by the criterion of the majority laid out by an ethnic group in a certain area. And we're going to show through our evidence that a person who was an expert in the Vance-Owen Plan will be putting this forward. Cutilliero's plan wanted to focus on the municipalities, and that's when the "leopard-skin" term began to be used as leopard-skin ethnic group oases. The Vance-Owen Plan wanted to see a union of the republics and provinces, which were to remain provinces, and that's what happened. Bosnia was, in fact, divided into provinces. In the meantime, between Cutilliero's and Vance-Owen Plan, a broad campaign was conducted and all the suggestions were legal insofar as they were not solved by war, insofar as it was possible to reach a democratic agreement. Each proposal was thus legal, joining Croatia or Serbia: The federalisation or confederal association with neighbouring states, confederation within Bosnia and Herzegovina, a union of federal units, and union of republics, a union of provinces, the Swiss model, based on cantons. All of this was legal. All of this was discussed, unfortunately for over two years, for far too long, because innocent people suffered, and we can't get them back. They can't be returned. And I think that they are observing us now. Not a single proposal was for a unitarian or civil Bosnia-Herzegovina by people who don't understand the issue or by people who really have nothing to do or no awareness of this. Every proposal had to do with a division. You know we're going to call a witness who will give testimony here as to what Lord Carrington told him. When, at the Butmir airport, when they were going to negotiations at the Butmir airport, Lord Carrington, the first negotiator of the International Community told him: "If you don't reach an agreement very quickly, we're going to let you kill each other, destroy each other, and afterwards we'll come and we'll impose our own solution." You'll hear a witness who was told these things. Unfortunately, this is exactly what happened, although the Croats, the smallest people, who were unable to come to a decision on their own without agreement with these other two, because at the beginning of the war there were 17 of them and now there are only 10 per cent of them, whereas the number of the other two peoples was constantly on the rise and continues to be on the rise even today. So they really could not do anything on their own, the Croatian people. They had to wait for the agreement of the other two people. It's signed. They signed every peace agreement because every peace agreement ensured the survival and the sovereignty of the Croatian people. That is why such agreements would be signed, such plans would be signed, because every plan was good for the Croatian people. It guaranteed its survival. But Izetbegovic signed both Cutilliero's and Vance-Owen's plan, and after that he abandoned them because their appetite was just too great. And see now, the role of the international community again, we are going to call a witness about -- who will testify about Izetbegovic returning from Cutilliero's plan, which was signed in Lisbon, and Zimmerman, who was then the ambassador in Yugoslavia, told Alija Izetbegovic, "Whose fault is it for you having signed this?" Because he was complaining about the fact that the Bosniaks had received too little territory. And the ambassador, Zimmerman, said, "Who is responsible for the fact that you signed this? Whose fault is it?" How else could Izetbegovic have interpreted this other than by saying, "What I have signed does not have to be implemented by me"? Such lack of understanding, Your Honour, at that time, was fatal. Either local interests, local political interests, or particular political interests, governed this, the interests of the entire -- of all of Europe, in western and eastern -- in the western and eastern areas of influence, and this border followed the central part of Bosnia, more or less. It always followed the central part of Bosnia. I will illustrate this. The last such division within the framework of NATO in Brussels was worked out in 1993, and the line takes this direction. The influence of the orthodox faith, the border can be seen here. This map was made in Brussels under the auspices of the NATO fact, and you can see where this line comes to an end. It goes right through the central part of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's where it ends. And now that I have shown you this map, I will show you something else that has not been understood or something that is part of an attempt at deliberate deception. And this is evidence for us. It's called Paddy Ashdown's serviette, Paddy Ashdown's napkin. This is the story. In London, at a banquet where the victory over fascism was being celebrated - and this banquet was held on the 6th of May, 1995 - President Tudjman, who participated in the antifascist resistance as one of Tito's partisans and who reached the rank of a general in Tito's army, President Tudjman was invited to this banquet, and as you can see in this map that you have before you, he has -- he explained this line and how in 1993, he received this map from Brussels, and given that he is dead, he can't confirm this but this book will confirm this fact, he probably only drew this line whereas Lord Paddy Ashdown, in his own hand, interpreted this as follows, and he wrote down what suited him at the time probably, in the light of the 6th of May, 1995, he interpreted in this light, when the Washington Agreement was concluded, when Dayton had almost been concluded, he said that Tudjman wanted the division of Bosnia, and I don't know why this has been presented here. It was the 6th of May, 1995. So who is being deceived here and what do they want to show? This book is going to be translated and all of Tudjman's arguments will be translated too, and all the denials of Lord Paddy Ashdown too, who is now to become the new governor of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He's already been elected as such. All interviews and all the denials that the late President Franjo Tudjman forwarded with regard to his statement and the interpretation, that will be presented, and we will provide evidence to show that this is false. As you see, all these negotiations with regard to the division of Bosnia led to the division of Bosnia. Because in fact, there are two federal units in Bosnia and Herzegovina now. That's what constitutes Bosnia and Herzegovina. One federal unit is called the Federation of Bosniaks and Croats. It has its own government, it has its own constitution, its own army, and its own police force. It has its own constitutional and judicial system. And the other federal unit is called Republika Srpska, which has its own army, its own police force, its own judiciary. The only thing they have in common is the currency, although I'm not even sure about this fact. I think it's their currency, and that's the convertible mark. Now it's the euro, and it's backed up by the Republic of Germany. This all took place at the end of 1992. January, 1992, Vance-Owen's plan was signed, the Bosniaks and the Croats signed it. It was necessary to implement it. It was quite clear what the division of the provinces would look like and who the governors would be. This was January, 199 -- Herzegovina belonged to -- was to go to the Croatian province, but the governor -- Zijad Emirovic was elected as governor, January, 1993. The SDA party, at whose head was Alija Izetbegovic, understood that a division was taking place, and that it had to seize as much territory as possible. Who did it turn to? It turned to the weakest people, the Croats. It didn't attack at any place the Army of Republika Srpska, and it didn't dare to do so. It started a policy of Islamisation. Up until then, this had been concealed but now it was public. It Islamised the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It replaced the legal leadership from Sarajevo to Mostar. It replaced the legally elected authorities in the municipality of Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor. And through its one-sided, illegal act, it replaced Dr. Ismir Mehmedcehajic, if I have pronounced this correctly, but in any event, a doctor who was the President of the Crisis Staff in Konjic. It brought in Dr. Safet Cibo from Sarajevo on the 8th of March, 1993, who then behaved in a dictatorial manner, unified the municipalities into one, and that was the municipality of Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor, and this resulted - and it's still the case today - that in the fact that there are no longer Croats in that area. In Mostar, the legal leadership was replaced, at whose head was Dr. Hadziosmanovic, a democrat. He was a democrat by conviction, and he didn't agree to such a situation, but Emirovic did agree to such a case and he replaced him. But he was just a puppet in the hands of the mufti Seid Smajkic, who, like the other imams and hodzas and muftis, actively participated then in the Islamisation. The commander of the entire corps, Arif Pasalic, and Izetbegovic's close associate, Safet Orucevic, who until recently was the mayor of Mostar. The Defence will show and will produce evidence before this Tribunal that they provoked the war in Mostar, they did it. They carried out propaganda and gave orders to all the media and to all Bosniaks, they told them to leave their work, to leave school, and told them that they shouldn't cooperate with Croats. Up until that date, they had lived in a normal manner. It doesn't matter what the programme is in schools, whether it's organised by the HZ HB. What is important is that children go to school. It's important that they finish their education, that they don't miss out, and when the state is free and rich, then school programmes will be created. What's strange about this? But in the middle of the war, with all those refugees there, special programmes were being asked for. And who is going to make those programmes when there is no state in existence? We will provide evidence to show that these four received that task from Alija Izetbegovic, the task to implement this in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they succeeded in doing this. And then a replacement, another replacement was made. The then commander, Sefer Halilovic, was replaced. He was the commander of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina but he didn't agree with Islamisation and he came into conflict with Alija Izetbegovic. And that it rapidly started Islamising. This is something that we will show with this videotape, where everything can be quite clearly seen. Please could you show the tape, at the point where we stopped? We can continue there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you fast-forward a bit, please? So within the framework of the legal army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, with the framework of the 3rd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the El Mujahedin Brigade was formed, which according to certain estimates, had at least 3.000, between 3.000 and 5.000 men. Please stop the tape and -- in fact, it would accept everyone and educate them and train them and then sent them to form Muslim units. Please can you show it now? Could you rewind the tape a bit, please? And we need the sound, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point. That's fine. Right here. So please, the sound, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Alija Izetbegovic came here personally and inspected the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please could you stop the tape a bit? What they were shouting was, "Our route to victory, Islam jihad." Please can you continue with the tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are all military commanders. That's the flag of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Alija Izetbegovic is being introduced to them. He is being made familiar with the situation. Please stop the tape. Stop the tape. Please stop the tape. So you can see this facial distortion here. The man who is sitting next to Alija Izetbegovic is being searched for. That's why his face is hidden. And the people who are sitting there, who are with him, they are people who have come from Islamic countries. Please continue with the showing of the tape. We will provide evidence to prove this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the main sheik for the shariat rights. You can see him behind the person whose face is distorted. The commander of the 3rd Corps of Bosnia-Herzegovina is sitting next to Alija Izetbegovic. You can fast-forward now. Please fast-forward a bit. Those are all the lineups. These are all mujahedin. You can see how many of them there are. I don't want to tire the Trial Chamber with this right now. We will have an opportunity to show this to our witnesses -- through our witnesses. This was one of the biggest camps -- one of the biggest training camps in the entire world. Please stop the tape. Please stop the tape. Could you rewind, please? From here. Stop here. You can show it from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the commander for shariat questions, who is driving here, you can see him here, we will have this tape translated because it's in Arabic, but we were told that he is driving with a mujahedin and his face has also been distorted. There is a report which is being submitted on Tuzla, and he is with another commander, and the overall commander for all of them is of course Alija Izetbegovic. Fast-forward a bit, please. Stop here, please. Could you rewind just a bit from here? That's fine. You can show the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So again there is another distortion. According to the translation, we have been told that this was the prince and here on the left there is a general, General Mahmudin [phoen] of the 3rd Corps. You can see how hearty these relations are. I didn't manage to read that. You can fast-forward here. These are just prisoners in the picture now, but this is not important. Please fast-forward. They are going into action here. They are showing their weapons and so on, the weapons that they have. Stop. From the El Mujahedin detachment, such elite units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were produced. This is the 7th Muslim Brigade that you can see here. Please show the tape again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fast-forward the tape, please. And now there are various members here who are telling their positions and saying what the purpose of Islam is. This is a foreign person who is calling on all the Muslims to come and fight in Bosnia and Herzegovina, to defend Bosnia and Herzegovina. And in Croatian or Bosniak they are describing why the Mujahedin are there, what their objective is, what their task is, or, that is to say, what the objective or task of each Muslim in Bosnia-Herzegovina is. This is one of the training camps. Here we have a member. He's a Bosniak, he's speaking in Croatian, and he is giving his reasons and he is asking all Muslims to fight against Allah's enemies. But we'll produce evidence to prove all of this. This gentleman, I think he is a citizen of Yemen. His name will appear now. He was also speaking. So all of this is propaganda. This is where the cassette could be bought at the time. It is quite clearly stated here. Please stop here. Stop here, please, and could you please rewind it a bit. Just a bit more. That's fine, right there. Stop there and show the tape, please. You can show the tape now. He was a commander for the shariat questions. He is interpreting that they had come here for training. He was talking about the objectives of the fight. Very well. You can stop the tape. You can stop the tape. He was providing explanations here. We will obtain a translation and you will very clearly see what the objectives were of the BH army, that is to say, of the Mujahedin. They are quite clearly speaking out against the United Nations, against America, against the International Community, and you will very clearly see what their combat objectives were and you will see in which year this took place. He will shortly explain what the task of each Muslim is. You see I stopped the image here on a soldier from the UN, that is to say, from UNPROFOR. Let's carry on. Let's continue. And it is the duty of the Defence to challenge the Prosecution, which says that the Convicts' Battalion participated in aggression against the Muslims. This never took place, this cooperation between the Croatian army and the Convicts' Battalion. The Defence will show who the Tutici are, and you will hear members of the Convicts' Battalion who fought against the Tutici and who destroyed their reputation, and this brought shame on the members of the Convicts' Battalion. The Trial Chamber will hear that not a single member of the Convicts' Battalion never said that he was a Tutic for himself. The real members of the Convicts' Battalion never had any reason to present themselves because they were presented by the Convicts' Battalion. The Defence will call witnesses who will say how the Convicts' Battalion was formed, when, and who was in command of it. The Trial Chamber shall hear how the founder, or one of the founders of the Convicts' Battalion, was Mr. Mladen Naletilic and how at the beginning there were only about ten young men, and from those ten it grew into a battalion. Your Honour, you will hear that the Convicts' Battalion was a military unit which didn't have to and shouldn't have had to be ashamed of its acts, and you will also hear the reasons for which many presented themselves as members of the Tutici. You will hear about Mladen Naletilic and the reason for which he went to Herzegovina, after many years abroad, and you will hear about the importance he had during the Serbian aggression. The Defence shall challenge the Prosecution's evidence about events in October 1992 in Prozor, Stolac, and about the reasons and circumstances under which a conflict broke out between the HVO and the BH army. Just for the sake of an illustration, I will now show you something. This is the following part of my opening statement. As you can see, the 4th Corps of Mostar, on the 23rd of March, 1993, the commander Cerovac Midhat sent this to Arif Pasalic on the 24th of March, 1993: We are informing you that the situation in the zone of our responsibility is as follows: 150 members of the HVO have been captured. The town has been blocked. Life in the town is paralysed, has been paralysed. There have been -- we are continuing with arrests. As part of the implementation of this plan, which I spoke of earlier on -- my learned colleagues, please, no objections now, no tu quoque objections. The events before the 9th of May, 1993 -- I'll give the dates and the places and the number of Croats who were killed while this plan was being implemented, this criminal plan was being implemented by the army of BH. The Gusti Grab village, on the 29th of January, 1993, five men killed. Orlista, 23rd of March, 1993, four killed. These were all civilians. Trusina -- this is all in the area of Konjic, of Konjic and Jablanica. Trusina, 4th of April, 1993, 16 civilians were killed. Miletici, 24th of April, 1993, five killed. Bilivode, 27th of April, 1993, three killed. Susanj, 27th of April, 1993, ten. Ten Croatian civilians were killed. I'm not going to carry on, because now we're entering June, June, July, August, September, October, November. The Prosecutor, in his indictment, says that up until the 9th of May there was -- a conflict broke out and that the HVO carried out an attack, that the HVO attacked defenceless villages, inhabited by civilians. You have seen the power of that army and we're going to provide evidence here to prove this. Can you imagine that these 50 civilians, these 50 Croatian civilians who were killed, can you imagine that this was something that was not known, that it could have been concealed, that the HVO had not attacked the BH army anywhere by that date? And we're going to prove this in this Trial Chamber. The Defence is going to contest the Prosecution's allegation that the army was an armed force of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that the HVO was in a conflict with the BH army. Both the HVO and the BH army were armed forces which were in conflict, but they didn't attack villages inhabited by civilians, which is what the Prosecutor wants to charge the HVO with and wants to charge my client, Mladen Naletilic, with too, of course. The HVO started a number of attacks against the Bosnian and Muslim population - that's what the Prosecution alleges - in April 1993, just as in Ahmici, on the 16th of April. Can you see to what extent before -- can you see to what extent the BH army had, both in Central Bosnia and in the area of Konjic and Jablanica, to what extent the BH army had been active? And that at the same time, on the 17th of April 1993, the HVO, with HV forces, including the Convicts' Battalion, attacked the Sovici and Doljani villages, under the command, overall command of Mladen Naletilic, and forcibly moved Bosnian Muslims and destroyed their property. Sovici and Doljani are two wholes that can't be divided, and I'm going to prove this to the Trial Chamber. I will elaborate on this a little later. I will go into details of the Convicts' Battalion in Sovici and I will talk about what happened in Sovici on the 17th of April, and so on. The Defence is going to show, is going to prove, that Mladen Naletilic was not and could not have been the commander of all the units on the HVO side, of all the units which participated in the conflict, and it will show that he wasn't even a commander of part of the Convicts' Battalion, which participated in the conflict. The Defence will show that Mladen Naletilic did not order, did not implement, and did not participate in the forcible transfer of civilians, and we will also show that in April, no Muslims were arrested, neither in Capljina nor in Stolac, nor in Mostar. The Defence, with regard to this, will also show, Your Honours, that no Muslims were expelled, no Muslims were dismissed from their work, that the Muslims who were employed in institutions or in economic companies which functioned during the war, they remained there. They could hold onto their positions. They could hold onto the positions they had before the conflict. And the Defence will show that the Muslims left their place of residence because the SDA exerted pressure on them, the SDA party. Within that framework, we'll also provide evidence that Caritas took care of 30.000 refugees in Mostar alone, of course, at a private session, in a private session, with all the information. Contrary to what the Prosecution alleges, that the HV units started the conflict, started the attack, the Defence will provide evidence proving that it was the BH army that attacked the HVO on the 9th of May, 1993, and that the conflict which ensued was not a conflict directed against the Muslim civilians. The Defence shall also provide evidence that the Croatian army did not occupy Mostar, and neither did the HVO. It will show the origin of the BH army and HVO conflict in Mostar. It will provide evidence proving that Mladen Naletilic was not the person who conducted a campaign against Muslims. It is necessary to distinguish certain concepts here, that of the Prosecutor, who says that it was an attack on the Muslim population, although the conflict in question was that between the Muslim army and not an attack against civilians. The Defence has to provide evidence to challenge the Prosecution's allegations that the events in Mostar and in Sovici and in Doljani, and it will provide evidence to show that the objectives were not ethnic cleansing, nor was it the seizure or taking control of the municipalities of Mostar, Jablanica, et cetera, thus forcing the Muslims to leave the territory. And by all means, the Defence will show that Mladen Naletilic did not in any way act with such a goal in mind. The Defence will show that the events in Mostar, in which unfortunately there were many citizens who were killed, both Muslims and Croats, many civilians -- there were people who were tortured, maltreated, abused, but these people included Muslims, Serbs, and Croats. This was not the result of the implementation of ethnic cleansing, but unfortunately it was the inevitable result of an armed conflict in which everyone is a victim, in which individual crimes are committed. But crimes are not the objective, but the unfortunate, the sad consequence. A criminal has a first and last name and he can't be called a Croat or a Serb or a Muslim. He has his own name. His name -- he is called a criminal. Your Honours, don't forget that that army that had been founded had only been in existence for a year. Show me any army anywhere in the world that can organise itself in a year. What sort of discipline can we talk about here, and what sort of order, internal order? I can't present this here before the Tribunal. I don't know how I could try to do so. But we'll try and provide evidence to show you how this was the case and to show you what measures were taken to ensure that these units were orderly, because they were formed from people who were neighbours, from people who lived in the same street, and then they gradually turned into certain units. And they all like to be called ATGs, anti-terrorist groups, and they finished up at the Bulevar in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I'm afraid that we have to stop here, because the next trial will use this courtroom. If you did not finish your opening statement, tomorrow morning you could continue with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much. I think that I still have another hour. I would just like to inform you of this.
